subject: gov.policy
name: Digital contribution to the RELANCE 2026-2030 plan
position_start: Baseline not held
position_end: Under formulation: the digital transition ministry working out what it contributes to the national plan
note: a ministerial CASEM session on the ministry's contribution to the RELANCE 2026-2030 national plan; the plan text, the digital component, any budget line and any target are all unheld, so what is recorded is that the process is running and not what it will produce

subject: gov.policy
name: National digital territorial development plan to 2030
milestone: Plan under revision to a 2030 horizon
position_start: Not held
position_end: The authorities are revising the national plan for the digital development of the territory to a 2030 horizon, to narrow the divide in a country where the international telecommunications union put about 70 per cent of the population off the internet in 2024 (2026-09)
note: a revision under way rather than an adopted text; no draft, budget, target or adoption date is held

subject: gov.policy
name: Schema directeur d'amenagement numerique
milestone: Planning observatory launched from the plan 24 October 2025
position_end: The medium and long-term national broadband and digital-infrastructure planning instrument, adopted by decree in council on 3 July 2019, carrying a 2030 nationwide affordable-broadband vision. It was operationalised on 24 October 2025 with the launch of a geographic information platform built from it to map infrastructure and coordinate investment. No coverage target in the plan has a published measurement against it

subject: gov.policy
name: Strategie nationale de developpement de l'economie numerique 2018-2027
milestone: Ministerial diagnostic records the strategy in force
position_end: The national digital economy strategy runs to 2027 on five programmatic pillars, recorded by the ministry's own maturity diagnostic of the public administrations. The diagnostic is the repository's evidence that the strategy exists; the strategy text itself is not held, and no monitoring report against its pillars is published

subject: gov.legislate
name: Banking regulation law of 2026
position_end: The legislature adopted a new banking regulation law on 26 June 2026, transposing the monetary union's 2023 uniform banking law and expressly extending its scope to financial technology companies and to new payment and electronic-money operations. It moves the domestic payments framework beyond the central bank's instruction; it was not promulgated at the date of the account, and no implementing text is held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Enforcement decrees under the 2021 law
position_start: Absent, with the commission pleading for their adoption to the Prime Minister in March 2025
position_end: Still never issued when the commission was superseded in August 2026
note: publication of any implementing decree, or its express abrogation, would settle it

subject: gov.legislate
name: Fast-track procurement decree
position_start: A fast-track procurement route with loose conditions of recourse
position_end: Recourse restricted to national sovereignty, strategic character, grave threat to public order, security or service continuity, and humanitarian consequences of insecurity
note: a rereading required by the revolutionary charter adopted in April 2026; the digital ministry has used this route repeatedly

subject: gov.legislate
name: Headquarters-localisation decree
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Firms above a revenue threshold must build headquarters in-country, with building standards set by revenue band
sources: 2026-02-13 Burkina Faso Orders Large Firms to Build Local Headquarters
note: the built-environment counterpart to data localisation, and it hits the three mobile operators

subject: gov.legislate
name: Information-systems security law
position_start: In force since July 2024, with the auditor-accreditation duty asserted without machinery
position_end: Now carrying a decree identifying, classifying and setting obligations for critical-infrastructure bodies, plus a decree fixing periodic audits and auditor accreditation
note: the mapping instrument lands before the biometric enrolment it will have to cover

subject: gov.legislate
name: Loi 045-2009 on electronic transactions
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: In force as the principal electronic-transactions statute, covering information-society services, electronic signatures, electronic commerce and distance-contract consumer protection

subject: gov.legislate
name: Whistleblower protection law
milestone: In preparation by the justice ministry
position_start: Carried by the justice minister, in preparation
position_end: No held source records adoption or any further step in the eighteen months since

subject: gov.protect
name: Data protection commission
position_start: An operating authority with no repressive powers, its standing borrowed from a prime-ministerial compliance campaign
position_end: Superseded as data-protection supervisor on the face of the August 2026 votes, never having received the enforcement decrees it asked for in March 2025

subject: gov.protect
name: Data protection law of 2021
position_start: In force as the operative statute with an annual-reporting duty, and no repressive powers because the implementing decrees were never made
position_end: Still the operative text, since the successor voted in August 2026 is not promulgated, and the decrees were never issued in the five years the law ran
note: the gazetted law is now held in its own right, where the repository had carried it through commentary

subject: gov.protect
name: Data protection law of 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Voted with processing without consent prohibited and sanctioned, administrative fines indexed to turnover and scaled by gravity, transfer of sensitive data abroad prohibited, use of personal data for commercial prospecting prohibited without prior consent and enforced by administrative sanctions of the regulator without prejudice to court action, and private video-surveillance devices left lawful but framed where they face the public highway
note: no text, number or gazette reference held; it must clear conformity review before promulgation

subject: gov.protect
name: Data-protection authority annual report
milestone: Validated in plenary June 2025, not published
position_start: Validated at the authority's sixth plenary session, unpublished
position_end: Still not found published as at 2026-07-25, against the statutory reporting duty, and a press-freedom body recorded that no report was made public for 2024
note: publication on the authority's site would settle it

subject: gov.protect
name: Merged communication and data-protection authority
status: In development, organic law voted awaiting promulgation
position_start: Did not exist; the broadcasting regulator and the data-protection commission were separate
position_end: A single authority merging the broadcasting regulator created in 1995 and the data-protection commission instituted in 2004, with its own rule-making power and staggered renewal of the first college, the state news agency placing the merger under the revised Constitution of 20 January 2026; no commencement, seat or leadership stated
note: nothing on file establishes how its independence, budget or appointment route is secured

subject: gov.protect
name: Non-profit register decree
position_start: A register governed by a 2017 decree with no retention period for the data it holds
position_end: Replaced under a 2024 anti-money-laundering law, fixing for the first time a retention period for the data after dissolution and adding donation declarations and intervention-theme fields
note: a surveillance register acquiring a data lifecycle

subject: gov.regional
name: Confederation data-protection coordination framework
position_end: The data-protection authorities of the three confederation states signed an operational roadmap for their coordination framework on 18 November 2025. It is the only practical cross-border personal-data mechanism the repository holds for Burkina Faso; it creates no adequacy finding, authorisation route or technical transfer channel, and the data-protection law voted in August 2026 prohibits transfer of sensitive data abroad

subject: gov.regional
name: Proposed fibre corridor with Nigeria
milestone: Proposed at a ministerial meeting, 12 August 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Nigeria proposed connecting its planned 90,000 km open-access national fibre network to Burkina Faso's borders to improve internet resilience, quality and affordability, alongside cooperation on artificial intelligence, digital public infrastructure and talent. It is a proposal, not a link

subject: gov.regional
name: UEMOA land registration harmonisation directive
milestone: Draft approved by eight member states, June 2026
position_start: No regional rule on land registration (2025-08)
position_end: Eight member states approved a draft directive harmonising land registration and titling rules across the union in June 2026, covering the establishment of urban land information systems; no domestic transposition is recorded (2026-06)

subject: gov.standards
name: Information-systems management procedures manual
position_start: A regulatory duty on every public service for more than twenty years, with no manual in existence
position_end: Validated as a harmonised reference framework for ministerial information-systems directorates, with formal approval by joint ministerial order not recorded as signed
note: signature of the joint order would settle it

subject: gov.standards
name: National object-identifier governance regime
position_end: The standards agency and the electronic communications regulator signed a framework convention on 4 February 2026 establishing a national object-identifier regime, designating the regulator's secretary executive as national registration authority and issuing a joint letter of recognition to the international telecommunications and standards bodies. It is the repository's clearest instance of a national addressing standard aligned to an international framework, and the technical building block the cybersecurity agency's public-key work rests on

subject: gov.standards
name: National standardisation, metrology and quality agency
position_end: A public administrative body with legal personality holding the national mandate for standardisation, certification, quality control and promotion, metrology and accreditation. It is the institution behind any national quality standard; the repository holds no catalogue of the standards it has issued and no information-technology or data standard among them

subject: gov.standards
name: Public digital platforms decree
milestone: Signed 2024-08-02 as a regularisation, deliberated in Council 2024-05-08
position_start: In force, requiring a prior favourable technical opinion before development or acquisition and a security non-objection before go-live
position_end: The same regime, with three sequential consents and an obligation on the supplier or in-house team to assign the full source code and current documentation before a platform goes into service
sources: 2024-08-02-burkina-decret-plateformes-numeriques-administration-publique|2026-02-19-decret-plateformes-numeriques-publiques|2024-05-13 Burkina Faso Revamps Public Administration with Digital Platform Decree
note: held as an image scan read by OCR; the decree itself says it is issued as a regularisation

subject: gov.discourse
name: Broadcasting regulator
status: Implemented, mandate transferred subject to promulgation
milestone: Communication-regulation mandate inherited by the merged authority
position_start: A standalone regulator of public communication exercising new social-media powers over users with 5,000 or more followers
position_end: Its regulation of public communication passes to the merged authority, putting broadcast-content regulation and data-protection supervision under one college
note: the merger removes the separation that let one act as a check on the other

subject: gov.discourse
name: Non-state consultation on digital law and policy
milestone: Roadmap validated with non-state actors 17 June 2026
position_end: Two instances, both documented by the state's own record. The legislature's sustainable development commission held formal hearings on 11 and 12 June 2024 with the internet society chapter, the federation of digital-sector associations and independent specialists during drafting of the information-systems security law. The artificial-intelligence roadmap was opened on 27 August 2025 with a situational-analysis workshop convening public institutions, the private sector, universities, research centres, civil society and financial partners into thematic sub-groups, and validated on 17 June 2026 with the same constituencies plus the diaspora. No standing consultation mechanism, register of submissions or response document is held

subject: gov.discourse
name: Organic law on social-media regulation
position_start: Extends regulatory powers to social-media users with at least 5,000 followers, with operationalisation started in 2024
position_end: Same; no held source records any change, and the enforcing body is folded into the merged authority
note: the only social-media-regulation instrument the repository holds for this country

subject: finance.budget
name: Data-protection authority appropriation
position_start: FCFA 499m appropriated for 2025, of which FCFA 480.3m committed and liquidated at 30 June 2025
position_end: FCFA 490m for 2026, down from FCFA 857m in 2024, a 43% fall over two years while the authority's remit expands
note: the only line in the repository with a 2025 outturn, because this section carries no external financing

subject: finance.budget
name: Digital transformation and ecosystem programme appropriation
position_start: FCFA 5,846m appropriated for 2025, of which FCFA 4,087m in a single chapter named after a foreign software vendor
position_end: FCFA 1,916,611,000 for 2026, with the vendor chapter gone and the ministry's whole domestic capital falling 72.7%
note: the volume removing the chapter was enacted five weeks before the sovereign-tools directive

subject: finance.budget
name: Digital-related domestic appropriation
position_start: FCFA 13,563m appropriated for 2025 across six tracked lines
position_end: FCFA 9,609m for 2026, back below the 2024 level
note: the total is the wiki's own compilation, not a published aggregate

subject: finance.budget
name: Domestic outturn at programme grain for 2025
milestone: Mid-year execution review published 2025-08-04, position at 30 June 2025
position_start: The 2024 annexe reported programme-grain domestic outturn across the tracked lines
position_end: The full-year annexe dropped the exclusion, but the mid-year review carries commitments by section and programme excluding external financing at 30 June 2025, when the state had committed FCFA 1,388.8bn of FCFA 3,199.5bn adjusted, or 43.41%
note: the mid-year review is not a settlement account, so the two years still do not compare at full-year grain

subject: finance.budget
name: Electronic communications infrastructure appropriation
position_start: FCFA 1,245m appropriated for 2025
position_end: FCFA 1,187,169,000 for 2026, the connectivity programme's third consecutive fall
note: the 2024 outturn on this line was 19.6% of appropriation

subject: finance.budget
name: Fast-track route for digital procurement
position_start: Used to authorise FCFA 5,895m of ministry contracts in July 2025
position_end: Conditions tightened by decree at the same council that used the route for a large schools package; FCFA 9,113m had been authorised for the digital ministry in April 2026, five times its whole 2026 domestic capital
note: which credits these draw on is never stated

subject: finance.budget
name: Identity-documents appropriation
position_start: FCFA 5,174,480,000 appropriated for 2025
note: the largest single tracked domestic digital line, and the one funding mass biometric enrolment

subject: finance.budget
name: Ministry work-plan execution
position_start: 10.80% financial execution at 30 June 2025 against 43.61% physical
position_end: 78.05% physical execution at 30 November 2025, with no financial-execution rate published for the full year
note: the 2024 comparison was 79.88% physical against 9.06% financial

subject: finance.new
name: Digital acceleration project
milestone: Latest implementation status report archived December 2025
position_start: A US$150m World Bank operation approved January 2024, effective September 2024 and closing November 2028
position_end: The same operation, framed at about US$170m with national counterpart, funding coverage of 1,000 localities in 2026 and expected to reach one and a half to two million people
sources: 2026-07-13-pactdigital-1000-white-zones-2026|2025-12-28 World Bank - Burkina Faso Digital Acceleration Project (PACTDIGITAL) Implementation Status Report|2024-01-23-wb-bfa-001-burkina-faso-digital-acceleration-project|2024-06-12-mdenp-pact-digital-bf-ratification|2023-12-22-worldbank-pad-digital-acceleration-project-p177022
note: two sizings in the repository, neither reconciled

subject: finance.new
name: Digital Transformation Fund country workshop
milestone: Fund presented to public administrations 18-19 August 2026; programme site published with eligibility terms
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A joint development-bank fund of 71 billion FCFA for digital modernisation of public administrations across the eight monetary-union states, presented to Burkinabe public administrations at a two-day Ouagadougou workshop run with the digital transition ministry, and since documented on the fund's own site with a six-step instruction and validation process, a named national focal point, and eligibility terms of a maximum 24-month project, a budget ceiling of 2,500 million FCFA, an interest rate the fund states at 2.2% and obligatory partial state co-financing
note: no national allocation, application or award is on record; the fund's own site puts the interest rate at 2.2% where a trade-press account of 2026-08-19 reports 2.77%, and the two are not reconciled

subject: finance.new
name: Financial inclusion and enterprise finance project
position_start: Running, with a digital-payments component of US$28.3m
position_end: Closed, with 81% of indicators met or exceeded, 280,000 people given digital financial education against a 275,000 target and 17,858 transaction-account users against 9,300
note: the coordinator sizes the whole project at US$110m, against a deal record carrying only the component

subject: finance.new
name: Private acquisition of a regional telecom operator with Burkinabe operations
position_end: A United States listed company announced a binding memorandum to acquire 51 per cent of a Ghana-headquartered group operating telecommunications and messaging-gateway infrastructure across six West African countries including Burkina Faso. Financial terms are expressly not disclosed, the country-by-country operations are not detailed, and closing is subject to due diligence and to regulatory approval in two other states

subject: finance.new
name: White-zone financing envelope
position_end: FCFA 75bn cumulative, half from the state through the universal-access fund and the acceleration project and half from the three operators, with lots allocated by reverse auction
note: not traceable to any line in the enacted finance-law volumes

subject: infra.connect
name: 800-tower white-zone connectivity plan
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: 800 towers are planned, 250 through the Digital Transformation Acceleration Project and 550 through the Universal Access and Service Fund, to connect 1,000 white-zone localities by 2027; the regulator's own figures put attacks on telecom infrastructure at 106 in 2022 against 11 in 2019, cutting coverage by 10 to 20 per cent
note: A plan with no contract, budget or site list on the record

subject: infra.connect
name: Cross-border frequency coordination protocol
position_end: Preferential frequencies for operators, interference-prevention mechanisms and 15 km coordination zones either side of the borders with three neighbours
note: signed alongside a separate free-roaming agreement

subject: infra.connect
name: Digital planning observatory
position_start: Recommended by a 2019 master plan, with ministry work to make it operational since 2023
position_end: A live geospatial platform on eight functional objectives covering network mapping, infrastructure sharing and duplicate-investment reduction, built to international mapping recommendations
note: the minister conceded primary-data quality and availability as the standing problem

subject: infra.connect
name: Domain-name security extensions
position_start: Not deployed
position_end: Cryptographic signing live on the country-code domain's records
sources: 2025-12-09 Burkina Faso Targets Online Trust with New Internet Security Measures (DNSSEC)

subject: infra.connect
name: Fibre and video-surveillance project
position_start: Under construction since July 2021 on a 54-month schedule
position_end: 650 km of backbone plus 150 km of city links, 900 surveillance cameras and 300 video-surveillance sites, on a Chinese concessional loan of RMB 560m
note: the two held records disagree on completion

subject: infra.connect
name: Interconnection catalogue 2026 to 2028
milestone: Published March 2026, revising the call-termination tariff framework
position_end: In force, with call-termination tariffs revised
note: known only through an operator's half-year filing; the catalogue itself is not held

subject: infra.connect
name: Internet exchange point
milestone: Peak capacity raised to 6 Gbit/s under peering support
position_start: Operating since June 2015 at a 6 Gbit/s peak, keeping local traffic flowing through subsea cuts
position_end: Operating at a 6 Gbit/s peak with local latency of 15 to 20 milliseconds against over 300 before peering
sources: 2026-05-25 Local Infrastructure Lower Costs How Peering Is Moving the Needle on Internet Affordability|2025-04-11 Local Businesses Benefit from Burkina Faso's Internet Development (BFIX)
note: no capacity update since May 2026

subject: infra.connect
name: National address-protocol migration roadmap
milestone: Operators and the regulator again call for a roadmap with a timetable
position_end: No adopted national plan or calendar on file, with individual operators migrating on their own schedules
note: a regulator or ministry decision adopting a dated migration plan would settle it

subject: infra.connect
name: National fibre network, deployed length
milestone: Reported in the ministry's 2026 work-plan presentation
position_end: More than 11,292 km deployed, with 270 km more programmed for 2026
note: no earlier cumulative figure on file, so the increment is not derivable

subject: infra.connect
name: National telecommunications backbone, first phase
position_start: 307 km in service at 1,600 Gbit/s
position_end: 307 km in service at 1,600 Gbit/s, the first phase of a stated EUR 175m and 5,740 km programme, with no phase-two status on file
note: financed by a Chinese buyer's credit after a European bank withdrew in 2019

subject: infra.connect
name: New public-administration network
milestone: Architecture finalised, pre-selected suppliers' bids under evaluation
position_start: Network reinforcement and further interconnection named as a priority, with 38 structures interconnected in the first half of 2025
position_end: Architecture of the replacement network complete and equipment procurement in evaluation, with the existing network operating since 2007 and 88 to 100 further buildings connected in 2025
note: the 2025 building count is given as 88 in one source and about 100 in two others

subject: infra.connect
name: Operator site-build commitments
milestone: Ministry follow-up meeting on operator commitments
position_start: 800 new sites planned for 2025 across the fund and the acceleration project, tender in progress
position_end: 2025 commitments delivered in full at 200, 200 and 150 sites across the three operators; for 2026 one operator is at about half of 100 planned and another has five live, twenty installing and 125 in build
note: the 800 planned and the 550 committed-and-delivered are never reconciled in any held source

subject: infra.connect
name: Satellite market authorisation
milestone: The minister says she hopes to rule soon on admitting the operator
position_start: No authorisation; the regulator declared terminal sales irregular under the 2008 telecommunications law
position_end: Still unlicensed, with ministry negotiations reported advancing and a decision pending
note: the operator's own continental map still listed the country as available from 2026 without a licence

subject: infra.connect
name: Universal access and service fund
milestone: Role restated at a regulator workshop, 29 June to 2 July 2026
position_start: Financing 500 of the 800 telecom sites planned for 2025, plus 50 more as zones cleared
position_end: Co-financing half the state's FCFA 37.5bn white-zone contribution, levied at 2% of operator turnover
note: no fund account published for any year from 2024 to 2026

subject: infra.connect
name: White-zone connectivity programme, first tranche
milestone: Service orders signed and equipment ordered 2026-04-04
position_start: Tender dossier for 750 localities finalised, project not yet launched
position_end: Most localities identified, service orders signed and equipment on order, with delivery targeted before end-2026
note: officially launched in September 2025, after the window opened

subject: infra.connect
name: White-zone connectivity programme, second tranche
milestone: Announced for 2027 at a working session 2026-04-04
position_start: Not announced
position_end: A second lot of 750 localities announced for 2027, with no separate financing line stated
note: the zero-white-zone-by-2027 framing sits against a 2030 full-coverage horizon for about 2,000 zones

subject: infra.connect
name: Wholesale price on the national fibre backbone
position_start: About 90 million FCFA a month for a 10 Gb service (2023)
position_end: About 35 million FCFA a month for a 10 Gb service (2026), on the operating company's own account of three years running the state-built 3,000 km backbone
note: the figures are the operating company director general's own in an interview; no published tariff schedule is held, and the 3,000 km here does not reconcile with the 307 km first phase and 5,740 km programme the repository carries elsewhere

subject: infra.store
name: Data repatriation programme
milestone: 120 externally hosted public platforms inventoried, migration begun
position_start: Not announced; the twelve programmes including this one were unveiled in August 2025
position_end: A localisation doctrine in force with 120 platforms inventoried, migration into the two national data centres begun and completion targeted before end-2026, the inventory expressly still incomplete
note: the minister's own statement that platforms may still be missing is the half that qualifies the count

subject: infra.store
name: Domestic commercial hosting provider
position_start: Did not exist; no wholly domestic commercial hosting provider on record
position_end: Operating with more than 600 domain names, more than 196 web hostings and 98% availability at launch, offering services from domain registration through virtual and dedicated servers to colocation
note: capacity, tier, certification and continuity are unstated, and the wholly-local claim is unverified

subject: infra.store
name: Government cloud
position_start: Not in service; its first datacentres were still under construction
position_end: In operation, its first two modular datacentres inaugurated at Ouagadougou under the zero-data-abroad programme to host, operate and secure all public data and to repatriate data still stored outside the national territory, with no capacity, operator or cost published by the government
note: its facilities are the two modular data centres carried as a separate row; the government's own statement publishes no figure of any kind

subject: infra.store
name: Government mini data centres
position_start: Under construction, with cost then given as over FCFA 15bn
position_end: In operation at about 3,000 terabytes combined, ten times the prior capacity, with more than 7,000 virtual machines at 100 to 300 per ministry, at FCFA 16bn and run by national teams
note: projected savings are stated two ways, about FCFA 30bn over five years and 85 to 95bn over ten

subject: infra.store
name: National big data centre
milestone: Announced for 2028 alongside the mini data centres
position_start: Not announced
position_end: Announced for 2028 to repatriate public and private data, with no cost, siting, tier or procurement on record
note: the mini data centres are explicitly framed as the interim step to it

subject: infra.store
name: Prime-ministerial circular requiring national hosting
position_end: In force and applied when hosting requests are assessed, since local hosting does not appear explicitly in the platforms decree
note: neither the circular's date, number nor text is held

subject: infra.store
name: Privately supplied modular data centre
milestone: Delivered to Ouagadougou by road from a Ghanaian port
position_end: A scalable modular data centre of 10 to 40 racks at 5 to 8 kW a rack, delivered to Ouagadougou by road from a Ghanaian port. It is the earliest physical storage-capacity addition in the window, ahead of the state's own larger facilities; the report sits behind a registration wall and only its opening paragraph is held, so no customer, siting or commissioning date is established

subject: infra.energy
name: Energy regulator's annual reporting
position_end: The energy regulator publishes an annual activity report covering its legal framework, institutional structure, regulatory approvals and technical and economic oversight of the national utility's production, transport and distribution assets. The 2024 report is the repository's primary document on grid reliability, and the capture stops before the chapters carrying the interruption frequency and duration indicators and the sector supply-demand deficit, so no reliability figure is held from it

subject: infra.energy
name: Energy supply for rural telecom sites
milestone: No named programme, budget line or target on file
position_end: Power is repeatedly named as a structural constraint on white-zone towers and the ministry says it is improving access to energy for sites, but nothing names an instrument
note: a fund or project document specifying site powering would settle it

subject: infra.energy
name: Thermal generation capacity added in 2026
position_end: Two plants entered service seventeen days apart. A 50 MW emergency thermal plant at Pabre was inaugurated on 21 July 2026, built in 90 days at FCFA 18 billion and framed by the head of government as a step toward production exceeding demand, with a further 120 MW plant broken ground the same day. A 26.4 MW plant at Bobo 2 was commissioned on 7 August 2026, raising that site from 60 MW to 86.4 MW at over FCFA 33 billion financed entirely from national funds and presented as reducing supply interruptions. Nothing states what any data centre draws or is guaranteed

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Critical-infrastructure classification decree
position_start: The 2024 information-systems security law in force with no identification, classification or mapping machinery
position_end: Decree adopted, defining critical-infrastructure bodies as any entity housing installations indispensable to society's vital functions, expressly spanning energy, water, health, telecommunications and finance
note: adopted at the same sitting as the mass biometric-enrolment decree it will have to cover

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Cyber agency appropriation
position_start: FCFA 498,036,000 appropriated for 2025
position_end: FCFA 489,236,000 appropriated for 2026, against 444,200,000 in 2024
note: the 2024 operations-centre licence and public-address lines do not survive the agency's move between ministry sections

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Cybercrime brigade awareness studio
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: The central brigade against cybercrime has equipped itself with an audiovisual studio to produce and broadcast educational content on digital risks, reported 8 September 2026; countering false information is central to the platform's remit, with audiovisual capsules devoted to deconstructing fake news and to information verification.
note: no cost, output schedule, distribution channel or audience measure is published, and no editorial safeguard is described for a police unit producing content about what is false

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Digital infrastructure supervision centre
milestone: Site inspected by the digital transition minister 2026-08-05
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A five-storey building under construction at FCFA 3.048bn, delivery scheduled for October 2026, to supervise the national backbone, secure cyberspace, manage state data centres and maintain critical infrastructure. At a ministerial site visit on 2026-08-05 the technical managers put physical execution across this worksite and the first Maison du citoyen together at about 20%, with the minister asking contractors to hold the pace
note: the August account names the build the Centre d’opération du Réseau Backbone national and gives it the same supervisory function; the repository does not state in terms that the two names are one building. The 20% figure is a combined rate for two worksites, not this one alone

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National cybersecurity agency's public-key foundations
milestone: OID sub-arc allocated to ANSSI, February 2026
position_start: No decree creating a national response team and no agency line naming one held
position_end: The regulator allocated an object-identifier sub-arc to the national cybersecurity agency in February 2026, a technical building block for a public-key infrastructure, certificates and electronic signatures; a national cyber-incident agency had been created in Council in July 2024. No incident response team is constituted and no advisory from either is on the record
note: Foundations for a signature service, not proof that a response team or an operating service exists

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Regional incident response centre
milestone: Named as a 2026 ambition at a ministry meeting
position_start: Not announced
position_end: Announced as an ambition for the regional confederation, with no host, financing or timetable stated
note: sits alongside a stated intention to pool digital infrastructure across the confederation

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Reported cybercrime complaints and losses
position_start: 3,028 complaints and 1.108 billion FCFA of losses (2022)
position_end: 6,367 complaints and 1.872 billion FCFA of losses (2025)
note: the cybercrime unit BCLCC's own figures, cited at a communications-council digital-security workshop for journalists and web activists held 27-29 July 2026 under law n°014-2024/ALT on information-systems security; complaints have more than doubled since 2022 and losses risen about 69%, but nothing states whether reporting propensity, unit capacity or the offence itself is what grew, and no clearance or prosecution figure accompanies them

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Security audit and auditor accreditation decree
position_start: The law asserted an accreditation duty for auditors with no procedure attached
position_end: Conditions for periodic audits fixed, and accreditation of auditors vested in the national cyberspace control body
note: the accrediting body is named by function, not by institution

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Security-product approval and homologation regime
status: Implemented, approval conditions not on record
milestone: Provided by articles 7 and 9 of the security law of 2024-07-09
position_start: In force by statute, with no implementing regulation on record
position_end: The same, with the decrees of 30 July 2026 fixing audit and auditor accreditation but not the conditions for technical approval or homologation, which the law leaves to regulation
note: importing or selling information-security hardware or software without technical approval carries a fine of FCFA 2m to 100m, at least doubled on repetition

subject: infra.cybersec
name: State digital platforms put through security testing
position_start: Baseline not held
position_end: 205 public digital platforms put through security testing against rising cyber threats
note: counts of platforms tested and bodies covered, with no period, no finding, no remediation rate and no naming of which bodies; the figures are the authorities' own, carried in a trade account

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Cross-border reservoir release protocol and flood data sharing
milestone: Protocol proposed at a bilateral meeting, 2 September 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Burkinabe and Ghanaian officials proposed a formal reservoir release protocol built on real-time data sharing and pre-agreed spill thresholds, at a bilateral meeting of a transboundary research project reported 2 September 2026. The Burkinabe power utility's chief hydrologist told the meeting that letters seeking closer coordination with the Ghanaian river authority, sent as far back as October 2025, had gone unanswered. Working groups mapped why flood warnings fail on the shared river: early-warning messages move too slowly, district assemblies lack transport and fuel to reach remote communities, agencies holding forecast data do not always talk to disaster responders, repeated false alarms have bred complacency, and on the Burkinabe side riverbank settlement is unchecked and inter-institutional coordination weak
note: a proposal from a research project rather than from either government: no protocol text, signatory, threshold or data channel is agreed, and the unanswered letters are the repository's only measure of how the two authorities currently coordinate

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Electronic travel form
position_start: Did not exist; airport embarkation and disembarkation forms were completed on paper
position_end: Forms filled online, with the border-police director stating that centralised data opens intelligence uses including movement analysis, anomaly detection and risk profiling
note: no retention rule or access control is stated in either account

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Identification and analysis platform for the internal security services
position_end: The council of ministers approved the development-operation record for a platform that builds on the computerisation and interconnection of five internal-security modules, covering judicial police, detainee management, civilian arms tracking and a mobile client, to pool identification data among security actors. It is approved and not built: no vendor, cost, timetable or data-protection assessment is held

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Interoperability of the national health information system
milestone: Disease classification implemented in four referral hospitals
position_end: The health ministry's procedures manual defines the national health information system with a central warehouse as its data store and expressly tasks the statistics directorate and other central structures with achieving interoperability between other databases and that warehouse, so interoperability is a stated objective and not a finished state. Two dated steps sit under it: a national roadmap co-created in September 2025 to integrate community health worker data from rural areas into the warehouse, and implementation of the eleventh revision of the international disease classification in four national referral hospitals over the 2024-2025 biennium

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Interoperability of the single social register
position_end: Funded and being designed rather than operating. A financier's appraisal document confirms the single social register exists and finances its planned interoperability with the unique identifier programme, the productive-safety-net project, the health insurance fund and the displaced-persons database through an application interface on the state payments platform. The financing, US$100 million of credit and US$20 million of grant, was approved on 15 June 2026 and expressly covers expanding the register's coverage and promoting its integration with those databases. The identifier itself is stated not to replace other administrative identifiers but to form their common digital base

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Referentiel general d'interoperabilite (RGI)
milestone: Adopted by Prime Ministerial order of 23 May 2018
position_start: No adopting order and no framework document held
position_end: The Referentiel general d'interoperabilite was adopted by Prime Ministerial arrete of 23 May 2018, fixing the rules ensuring compatibility between public administrations' information systems, and a training seminar on it was held in October 2019
note: A secondary account: the framework's own text could not be fetched from the ministry's server

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Subscriber identification against the national identity card
milestone: Government account of the 2018 decree to the legislature
position_end: A decree of 31 December 2018 makes identification against the national identity card a mandatory precondition for activating a subscriber card. It is the repository's clearest instance of the national identity credential being consumed by another sector's system; the government described the regime to the legislature in March 2023, which recommended strengthening it. No enrolment or rejection figure under the regime is published

subject: dpi.id
name: AES biometric identity card issuance
milestone: Special issuance operations launched at Koudougou
position_start: Not previously held by this repository
position_end: The national identification office launched special operations to issue the confederal biometric identity card at Koudougou on 9 September 2026, ahead of the seventh International Identity Day on 16 September. The card is the Alliance of Sahel States' common biometric identity document.
note: no enrolment target, issuance count, fee, site list or completion date is published, and the card's technical specifications have not been published by the confederation

subject: dpi.id
name: Code des personnes et de la famille of 2025
position_end: The 1,113-article code creates a national digital civil registry and assigns a unique electronic identifier to every natural person from birth registration or from entry into that registry. It is the legal basis for a digital identity from birth and it leaves the operational modalities to a subsequent implementing decree, which the repository does not hold

subject: dpi.id
name: Identity card as a condition of economic participation
milestone: Dependence on the card set out, July 2023
position_start: Not held
position_end: Possession of the national identity card is a requirement for most aspects of economic life, which makes issuance coverage an economic exclusion measure and not only an administrative one
note: the dependence is stated by a development partner and the card's own official description is held alongside it; no issuance coverage figure is published at any date

subject: dpi.id
name: Loi 027-2024 on unique identification and its enrolment decree
milestone: Enrolment decree adopted in Council, 30 July 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: The statute was adopted on 11 October 2024 and promulgated by Decret 2024-1261 of 28 October, in thirty-four articles; the Council of Ministers adopted the decree organising nationwide mass biometric enrolment for the unique electronic identifier under the WURI project on 30 July 2026, with fingerprint and iris collection under public control
note: No enrolment has been reported started, and no target population or timetable is held

subject: dpi.id
name: Newborn bracelet linked to a digital birth certificate
milestone: Every newborn issued a coded bracelet linking to a digital certificate
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Every newborn receives a bracelet carrying a unique code that links to their digital birth certificate
note: an implementing partner's account from 2022; no coverage share, facility count or later figure is held, and the repository's own registration-within-deadline measure is recorded separately

subject: dpi.id
name: Office national d'identification
milestone: Regional card adopted by decree 6 November 2025
position_end: The administrative public establishment created by decree of 15 December 2004, responsible for national identification, issuance of the national identity card, and the management, updating and securing of the centralised national identity database. It is the institution that maintains the credential and the database behind it. The credential itself is being replaced: the council of ministers adopted on 6 November 2025 the decree instituting the confederation's biometric identity card, available from age five and valid ten years, with a five-year transition for withdrawing the existing national cards

subject: dpi.id
name: Regional biometric identity card
position_start: Harmonised regional specifications validated by three security ministers in November 2024, with the older card still in issue
position_end: enrolment for the regional alliance's common biometric identity card opened at Arbinda
note: no enrolment or issuance total has ever been published

subject: dpi.id
name: Strategie nationale de l'etat civil 2023-2027
milestone: 2025 results reported to the steering committee
position_end: The steering committee reported for 2025 that the national civil-registration software was deployed in 30 main and 140 secondary centres, 78 main centres networked, 3,710,617 civil-status records digitised across 30 communes, and 128,051 birth certificates issued to previously undocumented and vulnerable people. Financial execution ran at 81.83 per cent and physical execution at 45.55 per cent, the gap between the two being the strategy's own account of what the money bought

subject: dpi.id
name: Unique electronic identifier
milestone: Enrolment decree adopted by the Council of Ministers 2026-07-30
position_start: A 2024 framework law in force with regional awareness workshops running, no vendor and no enrolment
position_end: Vendor recruited and a decree organising mass registration through national, regional, provincial and communal committees run entirely by public structures so that fingerprint and iris data stay sovereign, with mass enrolment targeted before end-2026
note: the 2025 tender failed; the decree states no enrolment target, budget or supervisory authority, and its gazetted text is not held

subject: dpi.id
name: Universal health insurance scheme enrolment
position_end: The universal health insurance scheme began paying benefits on 1 February 2026, requiring beneficiary registration and card issuance at a stated rate of about 3,000 cards a day at the managing fund, starting with civil servants in two regions before a phased national rollout. It is identity data being consumed by a social-insurance system; no cumulative enrolment figure is published

subject: dpi.pay
name: Certified electronic invoice
position_start: A 2017 paper standard was the traceability instrument until the founding arrete of 5 February 2025 set the conditions and terms for issuing certified electronic invoices
position_end: certified invoicing systems going on sale from 7 September 2026
note: The founding arrete is now held, as an image-only scan. The held sources state no mandatory date and no adoption figure.

subject: dpi.pay
name: Electronic tax filing and payment
milestone: Operational status confirmed on the state services portal
position_end: An arrete of 2021 fixes the legal and technical conditions for electronic filing and electronic payment of taxes, duties and charges through the revenue directorate's platform. The state services portal confirms the platform in operation for online filing, payment, case tracking and electronic tax certificates. No filing volume, digital share or taxpayer count on the channel is published

subject: dpi.pay
name: Electronic-money accounts
milestone: Reported in the central bank's 2024 digital financial services report
position_end: 9.53% of the union-wide 248 million electronic-money accounts opened at end-2024, fourth of the eight member states, with the national treasury one of only two treasuries among the 69 issuing initiatives
note: the report publishes the country share, not a national account total

subject: dpi.pay
name: National payments platform
milestone: Became the collection rail for automated traffic fines 2026-08-01
position_start: Government payments by application, web and short code, covering stamp duty, taxes and duties
position_end: The same, plus payment links for automated traffic fines, with vehicle immobilisation for non-payment within a month
sources: 2026-08-01-burkina-e-verbalisation-1099-infractions-en-12-heures|2026-07-30-burkina-faso-smart-traffic-cameras-ouagadougou|2025-01-30 Burkina Faso launches Faso Arzeka digital payment platform|2025-01-30-mef-faso-arzeka-plateforme-paiements-numeriques
note: the first case on file of a domestic payment rail carrying a coercive state obligation

subject: dpi.pay
name: Regional instant-payment rail
position_start: A real-condition test phase running, with a union launch announced for September 2025
position_end: Live, with nine domestic institutions authorised by February 2026 and 80 institutions connected union-wide by June 2026, connection deadlines pushed to September 2026 for banks and payment institutions and June 2027 for microfinance
note: the deadline extension is a union-wide decision, not a domestic one

subject: dpi.pay
name: Social security fund mobile application
position_end: A mobile application extending the social security fund's web platform, letting insured workers consult accounts and request pensions and payments, and letting employers pay contributions by bank transfer or mobile money. No download, user or transaction figure is published

subject: dpi.registry
name: Biometric electoral register
position_end: The Electoral Code establishes the independent national electoral commission, a biometric national electoral register built from permanent, annually revisable communal and provincial lists, and the national identity card or a birth certificate as the elector's proof of identity. The consolidated text held runs through the 2012 amendments and does not reflect the commission's dissolution in 2025, so the institution the code names no longer exists in the form it describes; no register size or revision record is held

subject: dpi.registry
name: Births registered within the legal deadline
milestone: Reported by the civil-registration modernisation directorate for 2024
position_end: 60.65% of births registered within the two-month legal deadline (2024), leaving nearly four in ten births undeclared in time
note: the figure is the modernisation directorate's own, carried in a partner programme document

subject: dpi.registry
name: Census population base
milestone: Definitive results of the fifth census published
position_end: There is no continuously updated population register. The definitive results of the fifth general population and housing census, enumerated in November and December 2019 and published in June 2022, put the resident population at 20,505,155. It is a periodic count, and it is the figure against which any dynamic register would be measured

subject: dpi.registry
name: Civil-registration platform
milestone: Registry officers trained on the platform in a rural commune
position_start: 3,391,907 civil-status acts digitised across 54 communes and 145,655 birth certificates issued in 2024
position_end: Thirty communes hold fully digitised registers, and 121,000 civil-status acts were issued to internally displaced people in 2025 against a 65,000 target. Delegated officers and transcribing agents in a rural commune were trained on the platform over 72 hours from 31 August to 2 September 2026, on smartphone configuration and real-time entry of births, marriages and deaths at central and secondary registration offices, organised by the civil-registration modernisation directorate and funded under a regional local-governance project in the 2026 budget year
note: a smartphone-based platform being taught commune by commune; no count of communes trained, officers reached or acts entered through it is published

subject: dpi.registry
name: Estate-agency register
milestone: Launched 2026-07-21 under an April 2026 interministerial order
position_start: Did not exist; brokering private residential leases required no licence and no register
position_end: A compulsory national card applied for and tracked wholly online, with a legally recognised virtual card issued on validation and a register the public can query, and commissions capped
note: no count of cards issued or applications received

subject: dpi.registry
name: Identifiant financier unique and the taxpayer register
position_end: Every user of the tax administration is assigned an eight-digit-plus-letter financial identifier recorded in the taxpayer register, and holding it is a prerequisite for banking, customs and public-procurement transactions. The register has been extended twice inside the window: an online document platform from June 2025 delivering the tax clearance certificate within 48 hours and taking those requests exclusively online from 1 September 2025, and certified electronic invoicing launched on 6 January 2026 and made mandatory from 1 July 2026. No count of registered taxpayers is published

subject: dpi.registry
name: Land and cadastre platform
milestone: Given statutory footing by an October 2025 law and a March 2026 decree
position_start: Online issue of land-occupation titles since March 2025, with a cadastral extract in one day and a definitive title in sixty
position_end: The same service, now the operating layer of a reformed land regime, with physical files no longer circulating between administrations and falsified titles rejected by the system
note: no figure for titles or extracts actually issued through the platform is published

subject: dpi.registry
name: Mining cadastre system
position_end: The computerised mining cadastre eMC+ under modernisation and expansion by its supplier on a World Bank-financed land and mining governance project
note: no delivery date or contract value is stated

subject: dpi.registry
name: National digital address register
position_end: No national digital address register, with an EU-financed municipal programme having numbered streets and doors in three of Ouagadougou's twelve arrondissements by April 2025
note: a national addressing instrument, or a register covering more than one commune, would settle it

subject: dpi.registry
name: Single social register
position_end: 362,698 households and 2,217,518 people, of whom 1,191,859 women, across 99 communes in ten regions, with about fifty further communes prepared for 2026
note: stated to interoperate with the unique identifier to prevent duplicates

subject: dpi.mis
name: Customs system
milestone: Advanced test phase, production described as imminent
position_start: Procurement of an intelligent customs solution authorised at FCFA 3.313bn, entirely state-budget financed, nothing built
position_end: The system in advanced testing with production imminent
note: no go-live date stated

subject: dpi.mis
name: District health information system
position_end: Rural clinics keep paper consultation registers which health workers summarise monthly onto paper forms for district teams to key into DHIS2, with tablet-based tools running in pilot districts alongside the paper registers rather than replacing them
note: the study measures district-level data quality, not national coverage

subject: dpi.mis
name: Employment agency job-seeker platform
milestone: Replaced pre-selection by lot from June 2021
position_end: Online recruitment for the public employment agency, ending the drawing of lots at pre-selection, and connected to neither a government data exchange nor any labour-market information system

subject: dpi.mis
name: National student registry
position_end: FIUE-BF enrols pupils and issues school identity cards, with national generalisation and interoperability set out in a strategy supported by the regional identity programme
note: no enrolment total is published

subject: dpi.mis
name: Pension acts platform
milestone: Announced as the completion of the pension programme
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Announced as the platform that will join the pension fund, the civil-service directorate and the budget directorate on a single pension file
note: no date, budget, vendor or scope stated

subject: dpi.mis
name: Solidarity platform
position_start: Did not exist; vulnerability alerts were reported late and information dispersed across actors
position_end: Assistance requests and tracking, complaint handling, solidarity appeals, financial contributions and statistical monitoring for social policy
note: no user, case or contribution figure published

subject: dpi.mis
name: Systeme d'information fonciere
position_end: A national land information system whose design, development and deployment started at a kick-off meeting on 9 December 2025, funded under a World Bank land and mining governance project and intended to centralise land data and its traceability beyond the cadastre and domains platform launched in March 2025. The account is the vendor's own; no cost, timetable or architecture is published by the state

subject: dpi.mis
name: Tax administration system
position_end: Tax administration sites interconnected over the state network around a single taxpayer identifier, with the 2025-2027 operational plan setting an action to upgrade the interface with the national statistics institute

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Administrative procedures live online
milestone: Reported at the 2025 objectives review, February 2026
position_end: 146 procedures operational out of 272 platforms initiated since the 2023 assises, with 69 new platforms built or started in 2025 and more than 270 procedures still in digitisation
note: the repository held no procedure count at the window's opening

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Automated traffic enforcement
milestone: Went live at midnight on 2026-08-01 after a pilot from April 2026
position_start: Did not exist; a 2023 system allowed digital payment of fines an officer had written
position_end: Live in the capital for four offences, with automated plate reading, interconnection to the vehicle database and the payments rail, a national supervision centre, and vehicle immobilisation for non-payment within a month. Its first month is measured: 19,910 offences recorded between 1 and 31 August 2026 generating CFA146.559m in fines, of which CFA16.1m had been recovered at the 4 September review - and a motorised police brigade was created on 2 September specifically to trace drivers who do not pay (2026-09)
note: a recovery rate of about 11% in the first month is what the enforcement brigade exists to answer; no appeal, error or contested-notice figure is published

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Central electronic-services portal
position_start: Did not exist; procedures sat on separate ministry platforms with no authoritative index
position_end: 1,672 information sheets, 95 dematerialised procedures and 183 public institutions on a single gateway, launched partly to counter fraudulent administrative websites, with a parallel citizen-petition platform
note: its 95 procedures do not reconcile with the ministry's own count of 146 live procedures at end-2025

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Certificates issued online
milestone: Reported at a national forum on the digitalisation of justice
position_end: Over 600,000 criminal-record certificates and nearly 70,000 nationality certificates issued through justice-ministry platforms, plus about 2,000 documents from a trade-register service opened in February 2026
note: set against internet access of 72% urban and 27% rural

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Diplomatic and consular service platforms
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Three launched: a diaspora registration and consular-appointment portal, an E-Protocole system for diplomatic cards, and a consolidated site for the ministry and its 52 missions
note: launched by the foreign affairs ministry; no user target, diaspora population figure, cost or supplier is published, and nothing states whether the consular services previously required attendance in person

subject: dpi.govtech
name: e-AGRÉMENT-MS health portal
position_start: Did not exist; health-establishment authorisation and partnership-convention procedures required in-person visits between services
position_end: In operation, taking online applications to open and operate private health establishments and for partnership conventions between the ministry and NGOs, associations and foundations, with applicants able to track a file's progress between services; built jointly with the digital transition ministry. More than 247 applications had been lodged since a soft launch in April 2026, of which 39 were validated at the official launch. No cost or timetable for further procedures is stated
note: the application and validation counts are the ministry's own, given at the launch; the 39 validated of 247 lodged is a completion rate the record does not explain

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Justice online services
position_end: Online criminal complaint and case tracking, a prison visit permit service and an online commercial register service, launched under a World Bank-financed 2025-2027 programme run jointly by the justice and digital transition ministries
note: joins an existing national electronic criminal-record service

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Loss of scanned scripts in automated marking of the 2026 recruitment competitions
milestone: Failure admitted and results corrected, 3 September 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: The civil service ministry admitted that part of one examination centre's scanned scripts were not carried over at the transfer from grouping to the marking machines in the 2026 recruitment competitions, affecting results published on 25 August 2026. After re-marking, 35 candidates were added to one training-cycle list and 39 to the health services managers list, none removed, and disciplinary measures were announced against those responsible
note: the ministry calls it human error; what the repository holds is a digitisation-to-marking handover with no reconciliation step, found only because candidates contested results, and no statement that the handover has since been made checkable

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Official-travel platform
position_start: Did not exist; official missions ran on a circuit made obligatory by prime-ministerial circular
position_end: All state-funded official travel including air-ticket booking must be processed through the platform, which identifies the most competitive offer automatically
note: locally developed, with no spend, saving or transaction figure published

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Online claims platform for seized property companies
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: The asset recovery agency opened an online platform on 3 September 2026, built with the state IT agency, letting people who bought plots or buildings from three court-seized property companies register their claims remotely and upload scanned identity and title documents, building a database the agency says will speed regularisation. Its director general stressed that it covers only property companies seized by the courts and placed under the agency's management
note: no claim volume, deadline, regularisation route or appeal mechanism is published, and the platform assumes claimants hold scannable title documents

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Pension formalities portal
position_start: Did not exist; pension formalities were handled on paper across three administrations
position_end: Online pension formalities, presented as improving data exchange between the pension fund, the civil-service directorate and the budget directorate rather than as a web front end

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Public platforms hosted abroad
milestone: First inventory disclosed at the Prime Minister's review 2026-07-25
position_end: 120 platforms inventoried, migration into the two national data centres begun and repatriation to finish before end-2026, with the minister stating investigations continue to find platforms not yet listed
note: no count existed before this one, and the inventory is self-declared incomplete

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Trade single window
milestone: Statutes converting the operator into a state company approved 2026-07-23
position_start: The platform operating since February 2016 under a company wholly owned by the chamber of commerce
position_end: The same platform, its operator converted into a state company on the stated ground of improving the governance of strategic digital tools
note: an ownership change to trade infrastructure, not a platform change

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Treasury platforms
position_start: Did not exist; the treasury deposit bank had operated since August 2024 with no online channel
position_end: One platform carries treasury teleprocedures and the other is the treasury bank's round-the-clock online banking, both built in-house and financed under a World Bank project
note: no user or transaction figure for either platform

subject: digital.localgov
name: Citizen service centres
milestone: First pilot, Zama Tchey, inspected by the minister 2026-08-05
position_start: A plan being drafted, with no site under construction
position_end: Two pilots under construction, the first of them named Zama Tchey and intended to bring postal, financial and digital services closer to the population, with architectural studies under way for a further city, eight regional capitals and fifty rural communes, against a state and postal-service contract for twenty spaces over five years; physical execution across this site and the digital infrastructure supervision centre together stood at about 20% on 2026-08-05
note: no unit cost and no beneficiary count published; the 20% figure is a combined rate for two worksites

subject: digital.localgov
name: Maison du citoyen (first site)
position_start: Not held
position_end: The first Maison du citoyen is 20% complete on a ministerial inspection of 7 August 2026, one of twelve structuring digitalisation projects the ministry names; the same visit inspected the national fibre backbone's network operations centre
note: no location, service catalogue, cost, completion date or count of planned sites is stated

subject: digital.localgov
name: Regional portals
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: One portal per region covering all seventeen regions, built jointly by the territorial-administration and digital ministries, with an electronic document-archiving system
note: an information and archiving channel, not a transactional service

subject: digital.rural
name: Commune-level civil registry digitisation
milestone: Registry agents trained on the national software at Koloko
position_end: The country's open government commitment sets digitalisation of civil-registry production and management and the creation of secondary civil-status centres in health facilities including in underserved and rural areas, on a timeline running to mid-2025. Two dated instances show what that looks like on the ground: 1,553 birth registers spanning 1950 to 2025 digitised in the rural commune of Safane in October 2025 by the national civil-registry modernisation directorate, and registry agents in the rural commune of Koloko trained in June 2026 on the national registration software, moving that commune from digitised archives toward active digital registration

subject: digital.rural
name: Digital migration data capture at rural border posts
position_end: Four rural border police posts equipped with a digital migration-data and document-scanning system were handed to the authorities in March 2024, built by the international migration agency. A further post at Galgouli was inaugurated on 29 October 2025 with the same system and five equipped patrol vehicles. It is data capture reaching remote posts through a border-identity programme rather than a rural digitalisation programme; no total of equipped posts, and no ordinary rural police station, is on the record

subject: digital.rural
name: Digitalisation of community and primary health facilities
milestone: Fifth assessment of the minimal digital ecosystem
position_end: The health ministry's digital health strategic plan for 2025-2029 documents the systems that exist, including the national data warehouse and a childhood-illness register reaching 84 per cent coverage, and plans digitalisation of peripheral facilities including rural clinics. A national roadmap was co-created in September 2025 to integrate community health worker data from rural areas into that warehouse. The pilot digital toolset across primary-care facilities in two districts was assessed in May 2026 with seven of its eight digital tools in active use and high-performing facilities nearly doubling from 23 to 44 of 72, with a recommendation to consolidate toward a national health intelligence centre

subject: digital.rural
name: Rural digital access points
position_end: Pilot digital access points opened in two villages in February 2026, equipped with computers and satellite internet and used by pupils and students for schoolwork in areas with no prior digital access. Two villages is the whole of what is held: no programme document, financing line, usage figure or expansion plan is published

subject: tech.ai
name: AI centre of excellence
milestone: A second competitive research grant began April 2025
position_start: A second phase running from April 2025 on about CAD 1m, after a first phase of CAD 1,057,100 from 2021
position_end: The same position, with the repository carrying no account of the centre since April 2025
note: the grant is in Canadian dollars, which the wiki's own pages render incorrectly

subject: tech.ai
name: Artificial intelligence in the health information system
position_end: A digital health-management system deployed in 86 per cent of primary health centres by the end of 2022 uses artificial intelligence to control data quality and to detect early signs of disease outbreaks inside the national health information system. On 29 October 2025 the digital transition and health ministries signed a collaboration agreement to design further tools for that system, naming diagnostic imaging support, epidemic prediction and a planned national health intelligence centre. No model, evaluation or deployment date for the new tools is published

subject: tech.ai
name: Automated enforcement detections
milestone: 1,099 offences in the first twelve hours
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: 19,910 offences recorded over August 2026, CFA146.559m in fines issued and CFA16.1m recovered (2026-08)
note: the ministry's own count, on the first day of operation

subject: tech.ai
name: Dedicated AI regulation
position_start: None published
position_end: No dedicated instrument; the justice minister told deputies the new data-protection law covers artificial intelligence notably through the prohibition on transferring sensitive data abroad, with the roadmap intended to become dedicated regulation later
note: a data-residency rule doing service as AI governance

subject: tech.ai
name: Francophone AI governance guidelines
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Common guidelines adopted by six states, led by an advocacy organisation, non-binding and complementary to national strategies
note: the text itself is not held

subject: tech.ai
name: National AI roadmap 2026 to 2030
position_start: No national AI strategy, with drafting not yet begun
position_end: A validated roadmap aligned to the national recovery plan under an AI-for-all banner, with a regional body counting the country among four member states holding a national strategy
sources: 2026-06-17-national-ai-roadmap-2026-2030-validated-techafricanews|2026-06-17-ia-feuille-de-route-nationale-validation|2026-07-14-sipen-uemoa-refondation-par-ia|2025-09-01 National AI strategy to guide Burkina Faso's digital transformation
note: the document itself is not held, and formal adoption or publication is not established

subject: tech.ai
name: Private AI institute
position_start: Launched as a private initiative, costed by its founder at about FCFA 100m, with two conferences held
position_end: The same, with nothing on file since August 2025 and its incubator and research centre still being structured
note: the founder's own cost figure

subject: tech.ai
name: Regional community AI strategy
milestone: A commission decision announced at a regional salon 2026-07-14
position_end: The regional commission to prepare and adopt a community AI strategy in a very short time, building on the four member states that already hold national strategies
note: no timetable, drafting body or budget stated

subject: tech.ai
name: Sovereign language-model corpus
position_end: A corpus build for four national languages, funded through a digital-transformation framework and named as a pillar of the roadmap; no dataset, size or release date published

subject: tech.industry
name: Domestic assembly of electronic equipment
position_end: One firm is identified as the country's first domestic assembly unit for computers, telephones and tablets, through a July 2026 equipment-access partnership with the public finances institute. It is the whole of the national production capacity the repository holds: no output volume, employment figure, local content share or plant description is published

subject: tech.innovate
name: Fabrication laboratories and innovation hubs
position_start: Not held
position_end: A described network of fabrication laboratories and innovation hubs supporting entrepreneurship
note: a 2023 landscape account; no hub count, membership, funding or survival figure is held, and nothing later reports what remains of the network

subject: tech.innovate
name: Innovation platform
milestone: Announced by the head of state October 2025
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A platform for inventors and diaspora innovators to register projects toward local manufacture, routed to an incubator described as under construction, with no operational statement or user count since
sources: 2025-10-24 Burkina Faso Launches Faso Andube Platform to Promote Local Innovation

subject: tech.innovate
name: Innovation ranking
milestone: Ranked in the 2024 global innovation index
position_start: 129th of 133 economies and 23rd of 27 in sub-Saharan Africa
position_end: The same, with the repository holding no 2025 or 2026 profile
sources: 2024-01-01 WIPO Global Innovation Index 2024 - Burkina Faso profile
note: the only comparative innovation benchmark the section holds

subject: tech.innovate
name: Multi-operator payments application
position_end: Over 400,000 downloads and a high store rating for a locally built application aggregating all three operators and five mobile-money wallets
note: the developer's own figures in a promotional account

subject: tech.innovate
name: Sahel Tech Innovation Challenge
milestone: First edition closed in Ouagadougou, August 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: The first edition closed in Ouagadougou having taken 600 submitted projects from 23 African countries down to 100, then 60, then 10 finalists; the first prize went to a Burkinabe agricultural artificial-intelligence tool built to work in national languages
note: No prize value, follow-on funding or second edition is on file.

subject: tech.innovate
name: Technology hub landscape
milestone: A third operator digital centre opened 31 July 2026
position_end: The only count the repository holds is a continental study of October 2019 identifying ten active hubs in the country. Two additions are dated inside the window: a privately run innovation hub focused on artificial intelligence and cybersecurity training opened on 23 May 2026 alongside an innovation competition, and an operator inaugurated its third digital centre at a university in Koudougou on 31 July 2026, extending the network beyond the two largest cities with artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, coding and incubation facilities. No current census, occupancy figure or survival rate is published

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Adult digital-literacy rate
milestone: No rate or baseline on file
position_end: No adult digital-literacy rate, financial-literacy baseline or school digital-skills figure is held
note: the one financial-education output figure in the repository comes from a project that has now closed

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Financial-education campaign with an operator
position_end: A partnership running since 2025 and extended in 2026 to four cities, with 72-hour sessions on budgeting, savings, credit and consumer protection and participants acting as community relays
note: consumer protection for a payments market delivered by a promotion agency and the operator, not the financial regulator

subject: capacity.training
name: Digital education in secondary schooling
milestone: 500 secondary-education actors trained across three regions
position_end: The education ministry's own orientation document of January 2024 is the adopted instrument and it records the state of play as unfinished across curriculum development, teacher training and distance-education infrastructure. Two dated deliveries sit under it: 167 secondary-school-aged girls given over 5,000 hours of hands-on training in programming, electronics, automation and video-game development in the second edition of a ministry and operator programme closing in October 2025, and 500 secondary-education actors trained in three regions in December 2025 in responsible and secure use of digital technology, on a cascade strategy stated to target about one million learners. No curriculum coverage figure, equipped-school count or trained-teacher total is published

subject: capacity.training
name: Digital skilling output for 2025
milestone: Reported at a ministry board, position at 30 November 2025
position_end: 169 young women trained in digital trades and 214 information-technology staff recruited into ministry directorates
note: no 2026 equivalent published as at 2026-08-05

subject: capacity.training
name: Lawmaker AI training
milestone: About thirty assembly members trained July 2026
position_end: About thirty lawmakers trained on artificial-intelligence fundamentals, applications and policy, to prepare review of future legislation

subject: capacity.training
name: Operator digital centre
milestone: Ministerial visit 2026-07-04, five years of operation
position_end: Five years running, with device-repair courses and a cloud-skills programme
